title: Market Positioning Statement
subtitle: Your team describes your product differently to every prospect. Your website headline
useWhen: changes every six months. Competitors are eroding your differentiation and you can't articulate a sharp, ownable reason to choose you.
howToUse: Al Ries and Jack Trout established in their 1981 work Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind that positioning is not what you do to a product, it is what you do to the mind of a prospect. Most businesses position by accident: they describe what they do and hope the right customer self-selects. Deliberate positioning works the opposite way you choose the customer, the category, and the comparison point, then build every word of your message to reinforce that choice. The goal is a statement so specific it automatically excludes the wrong customer and makes the right one feel it was written for them.
steps: Draft three positioning statements before deciding AI can generate all three.
Test each one: does it exclude anyone? If it appeals to everyone, it works for no one.
Share with 5 real customers and ask which one makes them lean forward.

Once locked, use it as the master filter for all marketing and sales copy. Oatly's positioning statement wasn't built around 'plant-based milk alternative.' It was built around a specific enemy: the dairy industry lobby. Their statement polarised the market intentionally , people who agreed with their position became advocates, not just customers. Positioning works best when it defines who you are NOT for as clearly as who you are for. IN PRACTICE The one sentence that tells your customer exactly why you not anyone else
origin: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind, 1981
promptBody:
Act as a brand positioning strategist.
My business                      :  [DESCRIBE WHAT YOU DO]
Target customer              :  [SPECIFIC ROLE, INDUSTRY, SITUATION]
Key competitors              :  [WHO THEY COMPARE US TO]
Our main differentiator  :  [WHAT WE DO THAT OTHERS DON'T]
Proof point                        :  [DATA, RESULT, OR CREDENTIAL THAT BACKS IT UP]
Write 3 positioning statements in this format:
For [TARGET CUSTOMER] who [PROBLEM OR NEED], [PRODUCT] is the [CATEGORY] 
that [KEY BENEFIT] because [REASON TO BELIEVE].
Make each one distinct  not just different words for the same idea.
Vary the angle of differentiation. Then recommend which of the three is sharpest and why.

proTip:
After writing your positioning statement, do a simple test: remove your company name
and replace it with a competitor's. If the statement still works for them, you don't have a
positioning,  you have a category description. Push harder on the 'because' clause. That's
where real differentiation lives.
